page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-1xCPU-4GB is an entry-level virtual server based on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this server is positioned for low-intensity workloads. The shared CPU allocation results in poor multi-core and single-core stress-ng performance, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested instances. While Geekbench single-core scores show a top-tier result, overall processing capabilities are constrained, as evidenced by weak multi-core performance and poor results in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write speeds categorized in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require continuous, high-performance compute resources. The shared-core architecture makes it suitable for lightweight applications, basic text processing, simple bzip3 decompression tasks, and development or testing environments. It is not recommended for database operations, high-throughput web serving, or resource-intensive tasks due to its low memory bandwidth and constrained CPU performance.
